name: Lion
blurb: ~190 kg big cat with a powerful bite and sharp claws
fact: A lion's roar is so loud you can hear it from five miles away.

name: Tiger
blurb: ~260 kg, the largest living cat; very strong, a skilled solo hunter
fact: Every tiger's stripes are different, like a fingerprint.

name: Grizzly Bear
blurb: ~360 kg bear with huge paws, long claws and thick fur
fact: Despite its size, a grizzly can run faster than any human sprinter.

name: Wolf
blurb: ~45 kg wild dog with great stamina and a strong bite
fact: Wolves live in family packs and howl to talk to each other.

name: Elephant
blurb: ~5,000 kg, the largest land animal; enormous strength and tusks
fact: It is the largest land animal and 'hears' through its feet.

name: Rhinoceros
blurb: ~2,000 kg heavyweight with a big horn and very thick skin
fact: Its horn is made of keratin, the same stuff as your fingernails.

name: Hippopotamus
blurb: ~1,500 kg; huge jaws, surprisingly fast, at home in rivers and on land
fact: It makes its own pink 'sunscreen' to protect its skin.

name: Gorilla
blurb: ~180 kg great ape with enormous arm strength and a powerful grip
fact: Gorillas share almost all of their DNA with humans and can learn sign language.

name: Cheetah
blurb: ~55 kg, the fastest land animal (110 km/h), built for speed rather than fighting
fact: It is the fastest runner on land and goes 0 to 60 in three seconds.

name: Crocodile
blurb: ~500 kg reptile with armored scales and one of the strongest bites of any animal
fact: Crocodiles have barely changed since the time of the dinosaurs.

name: Komodo Dragon
blurb: ~80 kg, the largest lizard, with a venomous bite
fact: It is the world's largest lizard and can smell food from miles away.

name: Wolverine
blurb: ~15 kg, famously fearless and strong for its size
fact: This little animal is strong enough to drag prey many times its own size.

name: Honey Badger
blurb: ~12 kg, famously fearless, with thick loose skin
fact: Its loose, thick skin lets it shrug off bee stings and snake bites.

name: Giraffe
blurb: ~1,200 kg, the tallest animal, with a very powerful kick
fact: It is the tallest animal, and its tongue is nearly two feet long.

name: Zebra
blurb: ~300 kg wild horse with a strong kick and bite
fact: No two zebras have the same stripe pattern.

name: Moose
blurb: ~500 kg deer with huge antlers and strong hooves
fact: It is the biggest deer in the world and can dive underwater for plants.

name: Boar
blurb: ~90 kg wild pig with sharp tusks, a fast charger
fact: A wild boar's sense of smell is even better than a dog's.

name: Tarantula
blurb: ~100 g spider; hairy, with a venomous but mild bite
fact: It can flick tiny itchy hairs off its belly to scare away enemies.

name: Scorpion
blurb: ~50 g arachnid with pincers and a stinger
fact: Scorpions glow bright blue-green under a black light.

name: Cobra
blurb: ~6 kg venomous snake that can rear up tall
fact: A king cobra can stand up tall enough to look a person in the eye.

name: Great White Shark
blurb: ~1,100 kg ocean hunter with rows of sharp teeth, top of the ocean food chain
fact: It can smell a single drop of blood from far across the water.

name: Orca
blurb: ~5,500 kg ocean giant: very smart, fast and strong
fact: Also called the killer whale, it is actually the largest dolphin.

name: Giant Squid
blurb: ~275 kg squid with 10 m tentacles and a sharp beak
fact: Its eyes are the size of dinner plates, the biggest eyes of any animal.

name: Piranha
blurb: ~3 kg small fish with sharp teeth; a single piranha is small
fact: Piranhas talk to each other by making barking sounds underwater.

name: Octopus
blurb: ~15 kg, very clever, eight strong arms, no armor
fact: It has three hearts, blue blood, and can squeeze through tiny gaps.

name: Barracuda
blurb: ~50 kg torpedo-fast fish with sharp teeth
fact: It can zoom forward in fast bursts to surprise smaller fish.

name: Electric Eel
blurb: ~20 kg fish that can give a 600-volt electric shock
fact: It can make a zap of electricity stronger than a wall socket.

name: Hammerhead Shark
blurb: ~500 kg shark with a wide hammer-shaped head packed with super senses
fact: Its wide hammer-shaped head lets it see in almost every direction.

name: Mantis Shrimp
blurb: ~0.5 kg shrimp whose punch can crack aquarium glass (tiny scale)
fact: Its punch is so fast it boils the water and sounds like a tiny bullet.

name: Blue-ringed Octopus
blurb: ~0.1 kg octopus with extremely strong venom but a tiny body
fact: It flashes glowing blue rings to warn that it is dangerous.

name: Swordfish
blurb: ~650 kg fish with a long sword-like bill, one of the fastest swimmers
fact: It uses its long pointy nose like a sword to slash through schools of fish.

name: Coelacanth
blurb: ~90 kg "living fossil" fish, slow and not a fighter
fact: People thought it died with the dinosaurs until one was found alive in 1938.

name: Bald Eagle
blurb: ~6 kg bird of prey with strong talons, small next to big land animals
fact: Its eyes are so sharp it can spot a fish from a mile away.

name: Peregrine Falcon
blurb: ~1 kg, the fastest bird (320 km/h dive) but small and light
fact: It folds its wings and drops like a missile to snatch other birds right out of the air.

name: Harpy Eagle
blurb: ~9 kg, the largest eagle, with a very strong talon grip
fact: Its talons are as big as a grizzly bear's claws.

name: Barn Owl
blurb: ~0.5 kg silent night hunter of mice
fact: Its wings are so soft it flies in total silence to surprise mice.

name: Hornet
blurb: ~5 g stinging insect; tiny
fact: Hornets build huge paper nests by chewing wood into pulp.

name: Dragonfly
blurb: ~1 g insect, an amazing flier but tiny
fact: It can fly backwards and hover like a tiny helicopter.

name: Albatross
blurb: ~10 kg seabird with a giant wingspan; not a fighter
fact: It can fly for years without ever touching land, even sleeping in the air.

name: Pelican
blurb: ~10 kg fish-scooping bird; not built for fighting
fact: Its stretchy throat pouch can hold more water than its own belly.

name: Crow
blurb: ~1 kg, a very clever bird; not a fighter
fact: Crows are so smart they remember human faces and use tools.

name: Army Ant
blurb: a single ant (0.01 g); in this game it fights alone, not as a swarm
fact: Army ants link their bodies together to build living bridges and walls.

name: Bombardier Beetle
blurb: ~1 g beetle that sprays a hot chemical puff; tiny
fact: It sprays a boiling-hot chemical from its rear with a loud pop.

name: Bullet Ant
blurb: ~0.03 g ant with a famously painful sting; tiny
fact: Its sting is named after a bullet because it is the most painful insect sting.

name: Praying Mantis
blurb: ~5 g insect ambusher with spiky front legs; tiny
fact: It can turn its head all the way around to watch you, like an owl.

name: Fire Ant
blurb: a single ant (0.005 g); in this game it fights alone, not as a swarm
fact: Fire ants can link into a living raft and float on water for weeks.

name: Centipede
blurb: ~30 g many-legged hunter with a venomous pinch; small
fact: Despite its name, no centipede actually has exactly 100 legs.

name: Wasp
blurb: ~0.1 g stinging insect; tiny
fact: Wasps invented paper millions of years before people did.

name: Stag Beetle
blurb: ~5 g beetle with big pincer jaws; tiny
fact: The males have giant jaws shaped like a deer's antlers.

name: Great Dane
blurb: ~65 kg, one of the tallest dog breeds; big and strong but a gentle pet
fact: Standing on its back legs, a Great Dane is taller than most people.

name: German Shepherd
blurb: ~35 kg working dog: strong, smart and brave
fact: Their amazing noses help them work as police and rescue dogs.

name: Golden Retriever
blurb: ~30 kg friendly family dog, strong swimmer and runner
fact: Their mouths are so gentle they can carry an egg without cracking it.

name: Labrador
blurb: ~32 kg sturdy, friendly family dog
fact: Labs have webbed toes that make them wonderful swimmers.

name: Husky
blurb: ~23 kg sled dog with amazing stamina and a thick coat for snow
fact: Sled-pulling huskies can run over 100 miles in a single snowy day.

name: Bulldog
blurb: ~23 kg stocky, muscular dog with a strong grip
fact: Bulldogs are too heavy and short to swim, so they need life jackets.

name: Beagle
blurb: ~10 kg hound with a super nose; small
fact: A beagle's nose has about 220 million smell sensors, way more than ours.

name: Poodle
blurb: ~25 kg standard poodle: athletic and very smart
fact: Poodles are one of the smartest dog breeds and were bred to fetch from water.

name: Corgi
blurb: ~12 kg short-legged herding dog, quick and bold
fact: Despite tiny legs, corgis were bred to herd big cattle by nipping their heels.

name: Pug
blurb: ~8 kg small, sturdy lap dog
fact: A group of pugs is playfully called a 'grumble.'

name: Dachshund
blurb: ~9 kg long-bodied hound bred to chase badgers
fact: Its long 'hot dog' body was made for digging into badger burrows.

name: Chihuahua
blurb: ~2.5 kg, the smallest dog breed; tiny but bold
fact: It is the smallest dog breed in the whole world.

name: Tabby Cat
blurb: ~4.5 kg house cat with sharp claws and quick reflexes
fact: The M-shaped mark on a tabby's forehead is part of its natural stripes.

name: Persian Cat
blurb: ~4 kg fluffy, calm house cat
fact: Its super-fluffy coat needs brushing every day to stay soft.

name: Maine Coon
blurb: ~8 kg, one of the biggest house cats; strong and agile
fact: It is one of the biggest house cats and loves to play in water.

name: Parakeet
blurb: ~35 g small pet bird; tiny
fact: One famous parakeet learned to say over 1,700 words.

name: Cockatiel
blurb: ~90 g pet parrot with a crest; tiny
fact: It can learn to whistle whole tunes and copy doorbells.

name: Canary
blurb: ~20 g songbird; tiny
fact: Miners once carried canaries underground to warn of dangerous gas.

name: Hamster
blurb: ~150 g pocket-sized rodent; tiny
fact: It stuffs food into stretchy cheek pouches as big as its whole body.

name: Gerbil
blurb: ~70 g desert rodent, a great jumper; tiny
fact: Gerbils thump their back feet on the ground to warn friends of danger.

name: Guinea Pig
blurb: ~1 kg gentle rodent; small
fact: When a guinea pig is happy it does a hopping dance called 'popcorning.'

name: Pet Rabbit
blurb: ~2 kg bunny with strong back legs; small
fact: A happy rabbit does a twisting jump in the air called a 'binky.'

name: Goldfish
blurb: ~50 g pet fish; tiny
fact: Goldfish can remember things for months, not just a few seconds.

name: Betta Fish
blurb: ~5 g colorful "fighting fish" that flares its fins; tiny
fact: A betta can gulp air from the surface using a special breathing organ.

name: Leopard Gecko
blurb: ~70 g spotted lizard; tiny
fact: It stores fat in its tail and can drop the tail to escape danger.

name: Cow
blurb: ~650 kg farm animal: very heavy but calm
fact: A cow has four parts to its stomach to help it digest grass.

name: Bull
blurb: ~900 kg, a very strong, fast-charging farm animal
fact: Bulls can't actually see the color red — they charge at movement.

name: Ox
blurb: ~1,000 kg strong working animal that pulls plows
fact: Oxen are so strong that people use them to pull heavy plows and carts.

name: Pig
blurb: ~150 kg farm pig: heavy and smart but not a fighter
fact: Pigs are very smart and roll in mud to stay cool, like sunscreen.

name: Piglet
blurb: ~10 kg baby pig; small
fact: Baby pigs can run and play within hours of being born.

name: Sheep
blurb: ~70 kg woolly farm animal; gentle
fact: Sheep can recognize and remember the faces of dozens of friends.

name: Lamb
blurb: ~15 kg baby sheep; small
fact: Lambs can stand and wobble around within minutes of being born.

name: Ram
blurb: ~100 kg male sheep with curled horns, famous for head-butting
fact: A ram's curly horns keep growing its whole life and have growth rings.

name: Goat
blurb: ~60 kg nimble climber with horns
fact: Goats are amazing climbers and can balance on the steepest cliffs.

name: Horse
blurb: ~500 kg, fast and strong, with a very powerful kick
fact: Horses can sleep both lying down and standing up.

name: Donkey
blurb: ~250 kg, tough and brave; farmers use donkeys to guard herds
fact: A donkey's loud bray can be heard up to two miles away.

name: Mule
blurb: ~350 kg horse-donkey mix, very strong and tough
fact: A mule is half horse and half donkey, and is great at carrying loads up mountains.

name: Llama
blurb: ~150 kg; farmers use llamas to guard sheep
fact: Llamas hum to each other and spit when they are annoyed.

name: Alpaca
blurb: ~65 kg fluffy relative of the llama; can kick and spit
fact: Alpacas have such soft, warm wool that it is woven into cozy sweaters.

name: Chicken
blurb: ~2.5 kg farm bird; cannot really fly
fact: Chickens are the closest living relatives of the mighty T-Rex.

name: Rooster
blurb: ~3.5 kg male chicken with sharp spurs on its legs
fact: A rooster can feel the sunrise coming and crows before it appears.

name: Duck
blurb: ~1.5 kg bird that flies, swims and floats
fact: Ducks have waterproof feathers, so water rolls right off their backs.

name: Goose
blurb: ~5 kg bird famous for being bold and loud; flies and swims
fact: Geese fly in a V-shape so each one can ride on the air made by the bird in front.

name: Turkey
blurb: ~10 kg big farm bird; cannot really fly
fact: Wild turkeys can actually fly fast, even though farm turkeys can't.

name: Border Collie
blurb: ~18 kg herding dog, super smart and fast
fact: Border collies are the smartest dogs and can learn over 1,000 words.

name: Dragon
blurb: giant legendary winged reptile that breathes fire, with armored scales
fact: In legends, dragons breathe fire and guard piles of golden treasure.

name: Unicorn
blurb: magical horse with a spiral horn and healing magic
fact: Legends say a unicorn's horn could turn dirty water clean and pure.

name: Griffin
blurb: lion-sized eagle-lion hybrid with wings and talons
fact: Half eagle and half lion, griffins were said to guard hidden gold.

name: Kraken
blurb: colossal legendary sea monster with enormous tentacles
fact: Sailors told stories of a giant squid-like beast that could pull ships under the sea.

name: Minotaur
blurb: bull-headed giant warrior with immense strength
fact: Half man and half bull, it lived in a twisting maze called the Labyrinth.

name: Werewolf
blurb: wolf-person with great strength, claws and fast healing
fact: In legend, a person turns into a werewolf under the light of a full moon.

name: Hydra
blurb: huge many-headed serpent whose heads grow back
fact: In legend, if you cut off one of its heads, two new ones grew back.

name: Phoenix
blurb: immortal fire-bird that is reborn from its ashes
fact: Legends say it bursts into flames, then is reborn from its own ashes.

name: Kitsune
blurb: nine-tailed fox spirit that uses illusions and magic
fact: This magical fox spirit grows an extra tail for every hundred years it lives.

name: Basilisk
blurb: king of serpents whose stare turns others to stone
fact: Stories called it the 'king of serpents' with a deadly stare.

name: Cerberus
blurb: giant three-headed guardian dog of the underworld
fact: This giant three-headed dog guarded the gates of the underworld.

name: Leviathan
blurb: legendary sea serpent as big as a ship
fact: This enormous sea monster from old stories was said to be bigger than a ship.

name: T-Rex
blurb: ~7,000 kg dinosaur with the strongest bite of any land animal ever
fact: Its bite was strong enough to crush a car — the most powerful bite of any land animal ever.

name: Triceratops
blurb: ~8,000 kg dinosaur with three horns and a huge bony frill
fact: Its huge bony frill and three horns made its head as long as a person is tall.

name: Velociraptor
blurb: ~15 kg feathered dinosaur with a big curved claw; quick but small
fact: Real velociraptors were turkey-sized and covered in feathers.

name: Spinosaurus
blurb: ~7,500 kg sail-backed dinosaur, longer than T-Rex, at home in water and on land
fact: With a giant sail on its back, it was the first dinosaur known to swim and hunt fish.

name: Megalodon
blurb: ~50,000 kg prehistoric shark, about three times the size of a great white
fact: This giant shark's teeth were as big as your hand.

name: Woolly Mammoth
blurb: ~6,000 kg ice-age elephant with huge curved tusks
fact: Its curved tusks could grow as long as a small car.

name: Saber-Tooth Tiger
blurb: ~400 kg ice-age cat with long saber teeth and powerful front legs
fact: Its huge fangs were as long as a banana.

name: Ankylosaurus
blurb: ~6,000 kg armored dinosaur with a heavy club on its tail
fact: It was covered in bony armor and had a heavy club on the end of its tail.

name: Pteranodon
blurb: ~25 kg flying reptile with a 7 m wingspan; light and fragile up close
fact: Its wings were as wide as a school bus is long, but it weighed very little.

name: Pterodactyl
blurb: ~5 kg small flying reptile; light and fragile
fact: It was a flying reptile, not a dinosaur, and ruled the prehistoric skies.

name: Dire Wolf
blurb: ~80 kg ice-age wolf, bigger than today's wolves
fact: Bigger and stronger than today's wolves, it hunted in large packs.

name: Therizinosaurus
blurb: ~5,000 kg plant-eating dinosaur with 1 m long claws
fact: It had the longest claws of any animal ever — as long as your arm.

name: Dodo
blurb: ~15 kg flightless bird, famous for being gentle and trusting
fact: This gentle bird couldn't fly and sadly went extinct about 350 years ago.

name: Thunderbird
blurb: giant legendary bird that commands thunder and lightning
fact: Legends say flapping its giant wings makes the rumble of thunder.

name: Manticore
blurb: lion-bodied beast with bat wings and a spiky scorpion tail
fact: It has a lion's body, a human-like face, and a tail tipped with spikes.

name: Sphinx
blurb: winged lion with a human head; strong, magical and clever
fact: In Greek myth, the sphinx asked travelers a tricky riddle to solve.

name: Chimera
blurb: lion-goat-serpent beast that breathes fire
fact: It is a mix of three animals: a lion, a goat, and a snake.

name: Wyvern
blurb: two-legged winged dragon cousin with a stinging tail
fact: A wyvern is a dragon with just two legs, often seen on old knights' shields.

name: Kirin
blurb: gentle but powerful sky-deer spirit with elemental magic
fact: This gentle creature was said to appear when a wise and kind ruler was near.

name: Roc
blurb: enormous legendary bird big enough to carry an elephant
fact: This legendary bird was said to be big enough to carry an elephant in its claws.

name: Jackalope
blurb: folklore rabbit with antlers; mischievous, not a heavy hitter
fact: This made-up critter is a jackrabbit with antlers, like a deer.

name: Baku
blurb: bear-sized magical creature that eats nightmares
fact: In legend, this dream-eating spirit gobbles up children's bad dreams.

name: Nue
blurb: monkey-tiger-snake spirit that summons storms
fact: It is a strange mix of a monkey's face, tiger's body, and snake's tail.

name: Ammit
blurb: Egyptian beast with a crocodile head, lion body and hippo legs
fact: It mixes the three scariest animals to ancient Egyptians: croc, lion, and hippo.

name: Peryton
blurb: winged stag larger than a horse
fact: It is a deer with the wings of a giant bird, casting the shadow of a person.

name: Zeus
blurb: king of the Greek gods, who hurls lightning bolts
fact: King of the Greek gods, he threw thunderbolts down from the sky.

name: Poseidon
blurb: Greek god of the sea and earthquakes, with a trident
fact: God of the sea, he could stir up storms and earthquakes with his trident.

name: Hades
blurb: Greek god of the underworld
fact: God of the underworld, he wore a magic helmet that made him invisible.

name: Ares
blurb: Greek god of war
fact: God of war, his chariot was pulled by four fire-breathing horses.

name: Athena
blurb: Greek goddess of wisdom and battle strategy
fact: Goddess of wisdom, legend says she sprang fully grown from Zeus's head.

name: Apollo
blurb: Greek god of the sun and archery
fact: God of the sun and music, he was said to pull the sun across the sky each day.

name: Artemis
blurb: Greek goddess of the hunt, a perfect archer
fact: Goddess of the hunt and the moon, she roamed the woods with silver arrows.

name: Hermes
blurb: super-fast messenger god with winged sandals
fact: Messenger of the gods, he wore winged sandals to zip across the world.

name: Hephaestus
blurb: Greek god of the forge who makes magical weapons
fact: God of the forge, he built magical armor and even robots out of gold.

name: Hercules
blurb: half-god hero with legendary strength
fact: The strongest Greek hero, he completed twelve nearly impossible labors.

name: Medusa
blurb: gorgon whose stare turns anyone to stone
fact: She had snakes for hair, and one look in her eyes turned people to stone.

name: Kronos
blurb: king of the Titans and lord of time
fact: He was the leader of the Titans, the giant beings who ruled before the gods.
